title: Buying Aluminum with DFARS and Origin Requirements: Questions for Suppliers
summary: Compare aluminum suppliers using the actual purchase-order requirements, quoted source, mill certificates, traceability and delivered price.
body_markdown:
## Check what applies to the aluminum item


Ordinary aluminum alloys such as 6061, 7075 and 7050 are not within the specialty-metal definition in DFARS 252.225-7009. Aluminum appears there as an alloying element in certain steels, not as a category of aluminum plate. A purchase order can still impose separate origin, domestic-melt, material or documentation requirements.


[DFARS 7009: scope and rules](https://www.acquisition.gov/dfars/252.225-7009-restriction-acquisition-certain-articles-containing-specialty-metals.)


## Ask for evidence tied to the quoted material


A supplier’s location, website language or general quality certificate does not identify the source of a particular plate. An MTR may include origin information; additional traceable source documentation may also be part of the required package. Assess the package against the order.


[How to read a mill certificate](https://noxmetals.co/blog/how-to-read-mill-cert)


Ask the supplier Confirm in the response


Which alloy, temper and product specification are you quoting? The complete material designation and required revision


Which origin requirement will this material meet? The required melt, smelt or manufacture country, as applicable


Which documents will accompany it? Mill certificate and any additional origin or conformance records


How will the material match those records? Heat or lot identifiers and traceability


What happens if the offered source changes? A revised offer and approval of any required substitution


## Compare suppliers on the same order


Compare the complete cut size, quantity, machining allowance, required documentation, shipping destination and delivery estimate. Ask about record access and any supplier approval required by your customer. An ISO or AS9100 certificate addresses a quality system; it does not replace material-specific evidence or the terms of your order.


## Choose the required origin option at Nox


Nox offers origin options for aluminum orders and includes mill certifications. Specify the origin your purchase order requires rather than assuming all stock is domestic. Review the quote and the final certificate package for the material supplied. A website option is not a certification of every clause in the customer’s contract.


[Origin and mill certificates](https://noxmetals.co/services/dfars-compliance)[Shop 7050 aluminum plate](https://noxmetals.co/materials/7050-aluminum)[Shop 7075 aluminum plate](https://noxmetals.co/materials/7075-aluminum)[Shop 6061 aluminum plate](https://noxmetals.co/materials/6061-aluminum)


## Avoid buying to an unnecessary restriction


Check the actual order and customer requirements before selecting an origin restriction. Commercial work and prototypes can still have specified origin or material requirements; the absence of a specialty-metals clause alone does not settle that question. Compare current quotes rather than assuming a fixed premium for an option.
